Subject: Post-demo: cost assumptions & batching questions

Thanks again for the demo today, Jordan 	6 really helpful to see the FastRetail checkout flow and where the model is used. As discussed, I summarized the key cost/throughput assumptions so we can align on a concrete next step. See answers below and an attached pricing sheet + sample traffic we discussed.

Quick recap of what you shared:
- Peak concurrent users during sale: ~1.2k sessions (burst to 3k for 10	615 minutes)
- Typical prompt size: 220 tokens in, 80 tokens out (average completion)
- Traffic pattern: long-tail (50% of requests are <200 tokens, 20% are 200	6500, 30% are >500)
- Expectation: ~10M	630M tokens/day initially, with steady growth if latency and unit cost look good

Questions / our assumptions for pricing:
1) Aggregated monthly target and runway 	6 you noted a $/1M tokens target range; can you confirm target budget range (e.g., $800	6$2,000 per 1M tokens) or a monthly commit target?
2) Batchability: you indicated that requests can be buffered for up to ~50	6100ms. That helps enable continuous batching; can you confirm that 90%+ of inference requests are non-interactive (i.e., can be micro-batched) vs streaming token-by-token?
3) SLA & fallbacks: any hard latency SLOs for p95? You mentioned 200	6300ms acceptable for interactive flows; we want to confirm for routing.

Prelim unit-econ estimate (rough):
- With continuous batching (50	6200ms batching window) and typical sequence lengths you provided, effective cost ranges we see on similar workloads are roughly $400	6$1,200 per 1M tokens depending on quantization and reserved capacity commitments.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the target budget range and percent of streaming requests
- We run a short traffic sample (attached sample CSV) through our sizing estimator to produce a committed pricing quote
- Schedule a 30-min follow-up with Marissa (pricing) and Aditya (inference arch) next week to review quote and procurement path

Attachments: 20260415-FastRetail-pricing-sheet.pdf (pricing + sizing), fastretail-sample-traffic-2026-04.csv (sanitized)

Thanks 	6 happy to hop on a call to walk through numbers.

	6

Thanks Camila 	6 great summary. A few quick clarifications:

1) Budget range: we're aiming for $1,200	6$1,800 per 1M tokens initially. That's for the first 6 months; if costs come down materially we can expand.
2) Streaming vs batch: ~85% of our calls are non-streaming inference (single-shot responses) and can tolerate a small buffer (50	6150ms). The remaining ~15% are streaming chat-like flows for customer service that need token-by-token streaming.
3) Latency SLO: for the checkout assistant we need p95 < 300ms (US region). For background personalization jobs, p95 can be >1s.

Also: on volumes 	6 initial pilot: 10M	615M tokens/day, with a targeted ramp to ~30M/day in Q3 if unit economics work. We can share sanitized daily traffic if that helps your sizing tool.

Happy to do the follow-up next week. Wed or Thu mornings PST generally work.

Jordan

Appreciate the clarity 	6 helpful. Two quick follow-ups and a preliminary unit-cost breakdown based on your inputs:

A) Confirmed assumptions used for the table below:
- Average total tokens per request: 300 (avg of 220 in + 80 out)
- Working concurrent baseline: 1.2k typical, burst 3k
- Batchability: 85% micro-batchable (50	6150ms windows), 15% streaming (no batching)
- Sequence length distribution: matches your long-tail notes

B) Estimated unit economics (high-level, ballpark):
- No commit (on-demand hosted): $1,750 per 1M tokens (this reflects reserved infra + higher per-unit runtime costs for smaller tails)
- 3	66 month reserved commit (dedicated pool): $950	6$1,200 per 1M tokens (depending on quantization & batching settings)
- Annual committed contract (Dedicated + aggressive quantization / 4-bit): $400	6$800 per 1M tokens (best-case with high batching efficiency and KV caching)

Notes on batching & concurrency:
- Continuous batching: with a 50	6150ms micro-batching window and 85% batchable traffic, we typically see 2.5x	64x reduction in effective GPU token cost versus purely single-request serving on similar models.
- Concurrency: For your 1.2k baseline and 300-token avg, we model needing ~2	64 dedicated GPUs for predictable tail latency at p95 <300ms with committed capacity; bursts to 3k would rely on autoscale / burst capacity (or fallback to slightly higher latency). Exact GPU counts depend on model family and quantization profile.
- KV/prefix caching: since you mentioned repeated prefixes in checkout flows, enabling prefix caching reduces effective inference work by ~10	625% on requests that reuse context, which lowers token billables for compute-heavy inner loops.

C) Suggested next steps:
1) Share sanitized daily traffic (CSV you attached is perfect) 	6 we'll run it in our sizing tool and return a proposed configuration + formal quote (Marissa will own pricing).
2) Book 30-min call Wed 4/22 10:00am PST with Marissa & Aditya to run through the quote and procurement path (proposed attendees: Jordan, Camila, Marissa, Aditya, one engineer).
3) If the quote aligns, we can spin up a short trial on Dedicated capacity for 2	64 weeks to validate p95 latency and per-token costs.

I'm attaching the quick pricing sheet we referenced; Marissa will take point on the formal quote.

Attachments: 20260415-FastRetail-pricing-sheet.pdf

	6
